title: Tulsi

seo.title: Tulsi (Holy Basil) - Benefits, Uses and Safety
seo.description: Learn about tulsi, or holy basil, including its botanical identity, Ayurvedic properties, traditional respiratory uses, benefits, dosage and safety considerations.

short_description: Tulsi is an aromatic sacred basil traditionally used in Ayurvedic teas and decoctions to support the throat, clear Kapha from the airways and ease seasonal cough and congestion.
full_description: Tulsi, or holy basil (Ocimum tenuiflorum, also known as Ocimum sanctum), is a fragrant leaf used as a household herb and in classical Ayurvedic preparations. It is traditionally considered warming, light and clearing, and is widely used for Kasa (cough) and Pratishyaya (nasal congestion), often as a fresh-leaf tea with ginger.

recommended_dosage.extract: Use only as directed by a qualified practitioner

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_effect: Traditionally considered balancing for Kapha and Vata; excessive use may aggravate Pitta.

key_benefits.benefit: Traditionally used to ease cough, sore throat and nasal congestion.
May help clear excess Kapha from the respiratory channels.
Used as a warming household tea during seasonal colds.

therapeutic_uses.use: Traditionally used for Kasa (cough) and Pratishyaya (cold and rhinitis).
Used in infusions, decoctions and steam with ginger or black pepper.
Used in traditional preparations intended to support respiratory comfort and immunity.

safety_and_contraindications.safety: Use culinary amounts unless a practitioner advises otherwise; concentrated extracts need professional guidance.
People with excess heat, reflux or Pitta aggravation may find large amounts too warming.
Pregnant people, those taking medicines, or anyone with a chronic illness should consult a qualified healthcare professional first.
